title: Four-day work week trials: what the evidence says
answer: Sample test data: in the trials summarised here, most companies kept the shorter week after the trial, and staff reported less burnout. Revenue held roughly steady, but the trials were voluntary, so the companies that joined may not be typical.

sections.heading: Did companies keep the four-day week?

points.text: In the sample trial, 56 of 61 companies continued the shorter week after six months, and 18 made it permanent.
Companies that dropped it most often cited customer-facing schedules that were hard to cover.

sections.heading: What happened to staff and revenue?

points.text: 71% of staff reported lower burnout at the end of the trial.
Revenue rose 1.4% on average over the trial period, which the authors call roughly flat.

disagreements.text: One review argues the results can't be generalised because companies chose to take part; the trial's organisers say the sample covered many sectors.

gaps: No long-term data beyond two years yet.
Few trials in manufacturing or healthcare.
